creator: nate.b.jones
title: One paste-in prompt that forces the AI into question-asking mode: ask me one question at a time until 95% confident, summarize why, state the plan in two lines, then wait for my signal (works on Codex, Claude, GLM, DeepSeek)
claims: AI defaults to 'be helpful and do stuff' mode and does not normally ask questions
Sequential one-at-a-time questions surface the model's hidden assumptions into the context window so you can correct them one by one
Helps most on complicated tasks; works on Codex, Claude, GLM 5.2/5.3, DeepSeek
how_to_steps: Paste before the task: 'Before you answer or do any work, ask me questions. Ask one at a time, strategically and sequentially, until you reach 95% confidence that you understand exactly what I am asking. Then summarize what made you that confident, write in two lines what you are going to do, and wait for my signal before doing anything.'
Answer each question; the clarified assumptions accumulate in context
Give the go signal once the two-line plan matches your intent
on_screen_only: Persistent title card 'AI Hack: Make Claude Ask Questions First'
cta: Let me know in the comments (none otherwise)

relevance.why: Cheap, immediate, and fits a time-poor founder: a few questions up front cost less than a wrong build. Maps onto the 'interview-me' skill seen in the honeycove video and the 'ask me 20 questions' step in the ads video.

implement_score.why: Turn this into a CLAUDE.md rule for non-trivial tasks or a /interview skill; 5 minutes. Pair with the phased-plan gate from youraveragetechbro.

verify: '95% confidence' is theater; the real value is the one-at-a-time constraint. Check whether Claude Code's plan mode already covers this for Haji's use
Watch for over-questioning on small tasks; scope the rule to complex features

gap.what: Liked set has mode prompts, Unlazy and Context Transfer, but not a pre-work interview prompt with sequential single questions, a confidence threshold, a two-line plan and an explicit wait-for-signal gate.
